name: TayzGrid
tagline: Alachisoft's Java in-memory data grid ported from NCache in 2013, with JCache; folded back into NCache.
description: TayzGrid was Alachisoft's native-Java port of its .NET distributed cache NCache, created in 2013 so Java shops could get the same peer-to-peer dynamic clustering, replicated and partitioned topologies, WAN replication, event notifications, MapReduce and a JCache (JSR 107) API. It also plugged into Hibernate as a second-level cache, Spring Cache and Java web sessions, and offered a Memcached protocol server for drop-in use. An Apache 2.0 open-source edition was published in 2015 alongside commercial editions up to version 4.6. Alachisoft has since dropped the TayzGrid brand, and its old product URL now redirects to NCache, which covers Java directly.
statusNote: Brand retired: the TayzGrid product page now redirects to NCache, which Alachisoft offers for Java and .NET. Use NCache, Hazelcast or Apache Ignite.

pricing.notes: Open-source edition plus commercial editions; the product is no longer marketed separately.

scale.notes: Partitioned and replicated topologies, with a WAN bridge between sites in commercial editions.

strengths: Feature parity with the mature .NET NCache engine at launch
Ready-made Hibernate, Spring Cache and web-session integrations
Dynamic peer-to-peer clustering without a single coordinator
weaknesses: Brand discontinued; open-source edition unmaintained since 2015
Small Java community compared with Hazelcast or Ignite
A cache, not a system of record: no durable primary storage
useCases: Hibernate second-level caching in legacy Java apps
